Without knowing your distro or installation method, my best guess is either sshd isn't running or your firewall is blocking connections. One thing you can try is to use netstat to see if your computer is listening for ssh connections. Here's an example:

netstat -an | grep LISTEN | grep 22

Replace 22 with whatever port it's supposed to be running on. If you don't see something listening on that port, then sshd is probably not running. It may he something as simple as ”systemctl enable sshd && systemctl start sshd" or your distro may need to run a different command to get it running.

If sshd is running then I would recommend either checking your firewall rules or (temporarily) disabling your firewall to see if that will let you connect. An example is "systemctl stop firewalld" but again you will need to check the documentation for your Linux distro.
